classification: pre-registered trade-level concentration, execution and capacity audit of the frozen R377/R378 hold-30 centre; research-only
question: The hold-30 centre has passed curve-level, cost and parameter-platform tests. Can its trades actually be concentrated, filled and liquidated within the stated assumptions, and at what capital scale does liquidity become binding?

frozen_strategy.portfolio: monthly 60-day inverse-vol risk parity, 10% C cap, 15% joint equity volatility target, 60-day overlay at 15%, one-third equity-weight cap, gold 200-day trend defensive bucket

trade_scope.B_sleeve: rerun the frozen hold-30 variant under the same isolated engine, membership, costs and execution rules, and persist every trade record plus execution counters
trade_scope.portfolio: scale A/B/C trade P&L by holding-period average final defensive equity weight and sleeve weight; C also receives the one-third cohort weight
trade_scope.capacity: use the same trade composition but revalue each position at multiple portfolio capital levels against the actual daily amount of the entry and exit sessions

curve_reconstruction.rule: 2x final portfolio annual, Sharpe and MDD each reproduce R374 exactly at abs tolerance 1e-9

concentration.reason: same v2 concentration policy used for the prior multi-asset candidate; gross-profit shares avoid the 5x net-profit denominator distortion

execution.reason: no-slot and same-day-reentry counters are strategy behaviour, not failed executions; cash/exposure rejections are treated as hard misses

capacity.reason: positions should normally be no more than 5% of a session's amount, with a 10% hard tail bound, and no more than one day to exit at a 10% participation cap

decision_rules: All curve, concentration, execution and capacity gates must pass.
Capacity is reported at every declared capital level; the hard gate is 100 million CNY, not the highest level.
No parameter may be changed, no position count may be altered, and no new cost model may be fitted from these results.
Trade-level P&L is an attribution diagnostic, not a compounded account ledger.
No leverage, paper target, order or production change is permitted.
known_limits: A and C trade caches contain abbreviated records, so their capacity notional is reconstructed from the equal-position nominal size rather than from a full entry_value field.
The C sleeve uses three cohorts, each weighted one third; failing to apply that weight would triple-count C.
Industry classification is a current snapshot, not point-in-time.
Daily amount is a proxy for executable liquidity; intraday depth, order-book impact and market impact curves are unavailable.
The audit is a feasibility screen, not a guarantee that a broker would fill every order at the assumed price.
2x trade detail is the primary composition audit; the 3x result remains the curve-level R378 validation.
